title: 2012 AMC 12B Problem 3
statement: For a science project, Sammy observed a chipmunk and a squirrel stashing acorns in holes. The chipmunk hid \(3\) acorns in each of the holes it dug. The squirrel hid \(4\) acorns in each of the holes it dug. They each hid the same number of acorns, although the squirrel needed \(4\) fewer holes. How many acorns did the chipmunk hide?

solutions.text:
Let \(h\) be the number of holes the chipmunk dug. The chipmunk hid \(3h\) acorns and the squirrel hid \(4(h-4)\) acorns.

Since they hid the same number, \(3h=4(h-4),\) which gives \(h=16.\)

The chipmunk hid \(3\cdot16=48\) acorns.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let \(h\) be the number of holes the chipmunk dug, so the squirrel dug \(h-4\)
